placements.why: Nothing in the supplied strata (empty) covers organizational categories at all; this envelope's content — a named system-to-system swap (PostgreSQL to QuantumDB) treated as settled fact in both spoken and written form — is a decision about underlying infrastructure, not a Strategy, Product, or Organization matter. Minting a bare 'Architecture' strata gives it a durable home with no forced ancestor, matching the rule that a strata mint needs no parent minted first.
placements.title: Infrastructure and platform choices are recorded as their own organizational category
placements.frame: What underlying system or platform is being changed, and what tier of organizational decision-making does that change belong to?

placements.title: A database platform is swapped out as a settled organizational commitment
placements.frame: What system is being replaced, who is treating the replacement as already decided, and what commitments (timelines, ratifications) accrue to it as the decision repeats across channels?
placements.why: src-1 (spoken, 'We're switching') and src-3 (written memo heading) both name the identical PostgreSQL→QuantumDB switch as closed fact rather than proposal — conviction reads both decision-grade, relational/power reads both authority-ranking and informational. src-5's Q3 2026 timeline is a fact evidencing this same decision's execution horizon (conviction: decision-grade commitment-marker; value: conservation/security via a fixed schedule) rather than a theme of its own — per the grain test it joins the decision leaf it supports instead of minting separately. This is the recurring subject future envelopes about this migration will keep feeding, not a one-time measurement.

placements.title: Performance and cost gains are the standing currency for justifying platform changes
placements.frame: What quantified performance or cost benefit is being offered as grounds for a platform decision, and how firmly is that figure held (claim vs. ratified fact) as more such justifications accumulate?
placements.why: src-2 (spoken) and src-4 (memo) both state the same '10x' performance figure and cost framing as the rationale for the switch — power/relational reads mark both rational-persuasion/reward and market-pricing, and conviction holds both at claim-level (asserted, not yet decision-grade), distinguishing the justification from the decision itself even though both concern the same migration. This is a recurring rationale pattern (quantified benefit as grounds for infrastructure change) rather than a single fact, so it earns its own leaf rather than folding into the decision leaf.
